verses.english: Linked Discourses 14.13
Chapter Two
In the Brick Hall

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Dhātuṁ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññā, uppajjati diṭṭhi, uppajjati vitakko”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, an element gives rise to a perception, a view, and a thought.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā kaccāno bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Kaccāna said to the Buddha,
“Sir, regarding

verses.pali: ‘asammāsambuddhesu sammāsambuddhā’ti, ayaṁ nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhi kiṁ paṭicca paññāyatī”ti?
verses.english: those who are not fully awakened Buddhas, there is a view that they are in fact fully awakened Buddhas. Due to what does this view appear?”

verses.pali: “Mahati kho esā, kaccāna, dhātu yadidaṁ avijjādhātu.
verses.english: “It’s a mighty thing, Kaccāna, the element of ignorance.

verses.pali: Hīnaṁ, kaccāna, dhātuṁ paṭicca uppajjati hīnā saññā, hīnā diṭṭhi, hīno vitakko, hīnā cetanā, hīnā patthanā, hīno paṇidhi, hīno puggalo, hīnā vācā;
verses.english: An inferior element gives rise to inferior perception, inferior view, inferior thought, inferior intention, inferior aim, inferior wish, an inferior person, and inferior speech.

verses.pali: hīnaṁ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti;
verses.english: One explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals the inferior.
I say that their rebirth is inferior.

verses.pali: Majjhimaṁ, kaccāna, dhātuṁ paṭicca uppajjati majjhimā saññā, majjhimā diṭṭhi, majjhimo vitakko, majjhimā cetanā, majjhimā patthanā, majjhimo paṇidhi, majjhimo puggalo, majjhimā vācā;
verses.english: A middling element gives rise to middling perception, middling view, middling thought, middling intention, middling aim, middling wish, a middling person, and middling speech.

verses.pali: majjhimaṁ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti;
verses.english: One explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals the middling.
I say that their rebirth is middling.

verses.pali: Paṇītaṁ, kaccāna, dhātuṁ paṭicca uppajjati paṇītā saññā, paṇītā diṭṭhi, paṇīto vitakko, paṇītā cetanā, paṇītā patthanā, paṇīto paṇidhi, paṇīto puggalo, paṇītā vācā;
verses.english: A superior element gives rise to superior perception, superior view, superior thought, superior intention, superior aim, superior wish, a superior person, and superior speech.

verses.pali: paṇītaṁ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti;
verses.english: One explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals the superior.
I say that their rebirth is superior.”
